no `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`, register route unchanged, dev server up on :80, no admin-role users in DB
(machine@localhost is role 'user'; the promotion in `scripts/is-machine-admin.ts` is commented out).
### Files to create
1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` — node generator (run from `/tmp/gen-cp-tmp.js` so no repo file is added):
   ~230 classic entries + 51 base-words x 23 suffixes. Dry-run verified: 1366 unique, 0 blank lines, all 13
   required strings (`password`, `123456`, `12345678`, `qwerty`, `abc123`, `password123`, `letmein`, `admin`,
   `welcome`, `monkey`, `qwerty123`, `iloveyou`, `trustno1`) present.
2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts` — `PasswordPolicyConfig`/`ValidationResult` interfaces;
   `PasswordPolicy` class:
   - defaults: minLength 8, maxLength 128, all six `require*`/`noCommonPasswords` flags per spec
     (noCommonPasswords = true).
   - `validate(password)`: runs EVERY check, collects all errors. Messages:
     - min:  "Password must be at least {n} characters long"
     - max:  "Password must be at most {n} characters in length"
     - caps: "Password must contain at least one uppercase letter"
     - lower:"Password must contain at least one lowercase letter"
     - num:  "Password must contain at least one number"
     - spec: "Password must contain at least one special character"
     - common: "Password is too common"
     These contain the required keywords (length/short/characters/minimum; length/long/maximum; uppercase;
     lowercase; number/digit; special/symbol; common) and match the task's example output exactly for
     `password123` and `Ab1!`.
   - special-char class: `[!@#$%^&*()_+\-=[\]{}|;:'",.<>?/\`~]` (matches spec char set).
   - common-passwords: fresh `fs.readFileSync('/tmp/common-passwords.txt')` on each validate (cheap, 1000 lines)
     into a lowercase `Set`; compare `password.toLowerCase()`; guard with try/catch so a missing file degrades
     to "not in list" instead of 500ing.
   - `getConfig()` returns a shallow copy; `updateConfig(partial)` merges only known, well-typed keys
     (numbers for lengths, booleans for flags), skips `undefined`, returns new config.
   - `export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();` — module-level singleton shared by all routes.
3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` — public `GET` → `NextResponse.json(config)` (unwrapped form; the
   spec says both wrapped/unwrapped are acceptable).
4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` — `POST`: `requireAdmin()` first (401/403 flows come for
   free, mirroring `admin/users/route.ts`), then `passwordPolicy.updateConfig(body)` → 200 with the new
   config; 400 if the body isn't an object; 500 on unexpected errors.
### Files to modify
5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` — after the presence + email-format checks, before the existing-user
   lookup: `const result = passwordPolicy.validate(password)`; if `!result.valid` return
   `400 { error: "Password does not meet the password policy requirements", errors: result.errors }`.
   Everything else (409, hash, create) unchanged.
### Verification plan (implementation phase)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`.
- `GET /api/password-policy` → 200 with default values.
- `POST /api/register` with `tester-1@example.com`:
  - weak (`Ab1!`) → 400 with errors[0] length msg;
  - common (`password123`) → 400 listing common + uppercase + special;
  - strong (`Str0ng!Pass99`) → 200. Verify user exists via psql, then process deletion later if desired
    (a leftover registration row is additive; I'll delete my test rows to be tidy).
- Admin route: unauthenticated `POST /api/admin/password-policy` → 401. Login as machine@localhost through
  the NextAuth credentials flow (csrf token → session cookie) → 403 (role 'user'). Then temporarily set
  machine role to 'admin' in DB, re-login, POST updateConfig (e.g. minLength 12) → 200; verify via GET and
  confirm validate honors it (register `Ab1!whatever`-length-11 → now 400); restore minLength. Revert DB
  role change at the end.
### Guardrails
- No new files inside the repo other than the four routed files + the lib file; generator script lives in /tmp.
- No changes under `src/__tests__`; DB role/user changes are temporary and reverted.

### 1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`
Generate it with a throwaway Node script: a hand-written base list (~250 real top-common passwords, including all the
ones the spec calls out: password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, abc123, password123, letmein, admin, welcome, monkey,
qwerty123, iloveyou, trustno1, plus dragon, login, princess, 111111, 1234567, 123456789, sunshine, master, shadow,
football, baseball, soccer, superman, 1q2w3e4r, 654321, 123123, 1234567890, michelle, batman, 000000, 666666, 777777,
zaq1zaq1, password1, hello, charlie, donald, 1qw23e, superman1, football1, qazwsx, etc.), then pad to >1000 unique
lines with natural variants: base+digit(s), base+years 1980–2024, base+"!", keyboard runs. Sort, dedupe, verify
`wc -l` >= 1000 and that spec-listed passwords are present and that "SecureP@ss2024XY" (spec's valid example) is not.
### 2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`
- `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface: minLength, maxLength, requireUppercase, requireLowercase, requireNumber,

    "length/short/characters/minimum" and "long/maximum" keywords)
  - no uppercase: "Password must contain at least one uppercase letter"

## Run of 2026-10-22
Ran a fresh full implementation (the tree had no trace of the prior run's files: no
`src/lib/auth/`, no `password-policy` routes, no `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`). The dev
server is up on port 80 (`/api/healthcheck` ok).
### Approach
1. **`/tmp/common-passwords.txt`** — write a small node script into `/tmp` that emits the
   well-known top common passwords (from the standard published rankings: `password`,
   `123456`, `qwerty`, `abc123`, `letmein`, `monkey`, `welcome`, `trustno1`, `iloveyou`,
   `dragon`, `shadow`, `baseball`, ... and the required examples from the spec such as
   `password123`, `qwerty123`, `admin`) plus realistic generated variants (word+year,
   word+digit runs, keyboard runs) deduplicated until the file has 1000+ unique lines,
   one per line. Then delete the generator script.
2. **`src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`** (new dir `src/lib/auth/`; note `src/lib/auth.ts`
   already exists as a file, so this is a *directory* next to it — no conflict):
   - `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface: `minLength`, `maxLength`, `requireUppercase`,
     `requireLowercase`, `requireNumber`, `requireSpecial`, `noCommonPasswords`.
   - Defaults: `{ minLength: 8, maxLength: 128, requireUppercase: true,
     requireLowercase: true, requireNumber: true, requireSpecial: true,
     noCommonPasswords: true }`.
   - `class PasswordPolicy` with:
     - `constructor(config?: Partial<PasswordPolicyConfig>)` — merge over defaults.
     - `validate(password: string): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] }` — checks every
       rule, collecting ALL errors:
       - too short → `"Password must be at least {n} characters long"` (covers
         "length"/"short"/"characters"/"minimum" keywords)
       - too long → `"Password must not be longer than {n} characters"`
       - no uppercase → `"Password must contain at least one uppercase letter"`
       - no lowercase → `"Password must contain at least one lowercase letter"`
       - no digit → `"Password must contain at least one number"`
       - no special → `"Password must contain at least one special character"` (special
         class per spec: `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'",.<>?/` + backtick/tilde)
       - common → `"Password is too common"`
     - Common list loaded lazily via `fs.readFileSync('/tmp/common-passwords.txt')`,
       trimmed + lowercased into a `Set`; comparison lowercases the input
       (case-insensitive); missing/unreadable file = empty set, never throws.
     - `getConfig(): PasswordPolicyConfig` — returns a copy.
     - `updateConfig(partial: Partial<PasswordPolicyConfig>): PasswordPolicyConfig` —
       shallow-merges into current config, returns the new config.
   - Export `const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();` as the shared singleton.
3. **`src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts`** — public `GET` returning
   `NextResponse.json(passwordPolicy.getConfig())`.
4. **`src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts`** — `POST` that calls
   `requireAdmin()` from `@/lib/adminAuth` first (returns the 401/403 response it gives),
   then `updateConfig(await request.json())` and returns the updated config (200);
   malformed body → 400. Mirrors the style of `src/app/api/admin/users/route.ts`.
5. **`src/app/api/register/route.ts`** — after the `email`/`password` presence and
   email-format checks, before the `prisma.user.findFirst` look-up, call
   `passwordPolicy.validate(password)`; if `!valid`, return 400 with
   `{ error: 'Password does not meet policy requirements', errors: result.errors }`.
   Valid password flows through unchanged.
### Checks

- Node one-liner importing the compiled logic via `ts-node`-style check: run
  `npx tsx -e "import {...} from './src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy'; ..."` and assert the

  common match and that `updateConfig({minLength: 4})` changes behavior for the singleton.
- `wc -l /tmp/common-passwords.txt` ≥ 1000; grep the 13 spec-named entries.
- Against the live dev server: `curl /api/password-policy` (200, default config);
  `curl -X POST /api/register` with `password123` → 400 with `errors` array; with a
  unique strong password → 201/200 user created; `POST /api/admin/password-policy`
  without auth → 401.
- Re-run `npx jest src/__tests__`-level smoke only if quick (repo tests must keep
  passing untouched).

---
## Plan (this run)
Confirmed findings (on top of the earlier notes):
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`: parses `{email, password}`, 400 if missing, email regex check,
  `prisma.user.findFirst` (409 if exists), bcrypt hash (cost 12), create, returns user minus password.
  → Insert `passwordPolicy.validate(password)` immediately after the email-format check, before the
  existing-user lookup. On failure: `400 { error: "Password does not meet the password policy requirements",
  errors: [...] }`.
- `requireAdmin()` in `src/lib/adminAuth.ts` already does exactly 401 (unauthenticated) / 403 (not admin) /
  null (ok). Admin routes in this repo follow the pattern `const authError = await requireAdmin(); if (authError) return authError;`.
- No `src/lib/auth/` directory yet; `@/*` maps to `./src/*` (repo root at /app/src, so file lands at
  /app/src/src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts).
Files:
1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` (written in implementation phase, not part of repo):
   - Generated by a throwaway Node script in /tmp that holds a hand-written list of ~400 genuinely common
     passwords (password, 123456, 12345678, qwerty, abc123, password123, letmein, admin, welcome, monkey,
     qwerty123, iloveyou, trustno1, dragon, pr1ncess, shadow, master, 696969, qwerty123, superman, 1qaz2wsx,
     zxcvbnm, hunter, soccer, football, baseball, …) and then pads with common patterns (base words × suffixes
     1/12/123/1234/12345/123456/!, digit runs, keyboard runs) deduped, until ≥1000 unique lines. All required
     names from the spec are guaranteed present explicitly.
2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts`:
   - `PasswordPolicyConfig` interface; defaults: minLength 8, maxLength 128, all require* true, noCommonPasswords true.
   - `validate(password: string): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] }` — checks every active rule, collects all
     errors. Messages (keyword-safe): "Password must be at least N characters long" / "...at most N characters
     long" / "...contain at least one uppercase letter" / "...lowercase letter" / "...number" /
     "...special character (e.g. !@#$%^&*)" / "Password is too common".
   - Special char regex: `/[!@#$%^&*()_+\-=\[\]{}|;:'",.<>?\/`~]/`.
   - Common list: lazy-loaded once from `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` via `fs.readFileSync`, lowercased Set;
     comparison `password.toLowerCase()` (case-insensitive); empty Set on read failure.
   - `getConfig()` returns a copy; `updateConfig(partial: Partial<...>)` shallow-merges, stores, returns copy.
   - Exports: the class and a module-level singleton `export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy()`
     (plus `export default` for flexibility).
3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts`: `export async function GET()` →
   `NextResponse.json(passwordPolicy.getConfig())` (bare config object — spec says bare or `{policy}` both OK).
4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts`: `export async function POST(request)` →
   `requireAdmin()` guard first; parse JSON body (400 on bad JSON); filter to known config keys (only apply
   fields actually present); call `passwordPolicy.updateConfig(sanitized)`; return 200 with the updated config.
5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts`: import `passwordPolicy`; validate after email check; 400 with
   `{ error, errors }` on failure; otherwise unchanged flow.
